slot.brief: Compare de Broglie wavelength of an electron vs an alpha particle accelerated through the same potential difference (or same kinetic energy); derive the ratio from mass and charge.

stem: An electron and an α-particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Take $m_\alpha=4m_p$, $m_p=1836m_e$, and their charges as $e$ and $2e$, respectively. Neglect relativistic effects. What is $\lambda_e: \lambda_\alpha$?

verdicts.working: For the same potential difference, \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\). Thus \(\lambda_e/\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{m_\alpha(2e)/(m_e e)}=\sqrt{14688}=12\sqrt{102}.\)

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$
$\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_\alpha(2e)}{m_e e}}=\sqrt{8\times1836}$
$\sqrt{14688}=12\sqrt{102}$

Independent check: For the same potential difference, \(\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}\). Thus \(\lambda_e/\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{m_\alpha(2e)/(m_e e)}=\sqrt{14688}=12\sqrt{102}.\)
solution:
For a particle accelerated through potential difference $V$, $\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mqV}$.
$$\frac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha(2e)}{m_e e}}=\sqrt{8\times1836}=12\sqrt{102}$$
Hence, $\lambda_e: \lambda_\alpha=12\sqrt{102}:1$. (B)
